previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient, a man with long-standing epilepsy, end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis, and a history of stroke, was admitted after experiencing a generalized tonic-clonic seizure following a hemodialysis session. The seizure occurred in the context of significant fluid removal (4.5 L), post-dialysis hypotension (SBP 75), fasting for a scheduled colonoscopy, and failure to take his usual extra doses of oxcarbazepine and levetiracetam after dialysis. He had another witnessed seizure in the emergency department, which resolved with intravenous lorazepam. Evaluation included a CT head and chest X-ray, both showing no acute abnormalities. He received the missed antiepileptic doses and 500 mL of IV fluids. His condition stabilized, mental status returned to baseline, and he was discharged home after two days. Medications were continued without change, and he was advised to follow up with his neurologist and dialysis team, with emphasis on medication adherence, especially post-dialysis doses.
problems: Epilepsy, unspecified, without mention of intractable epilepsy
Personal history of transient ischemic attack (TIA), and cerebral infarction without residual deficits

radiology_notes.text:
HISTORY:  ___ male status post seizure at hemodialysis.

TECHNIQUE:  Contiguous axial images obtained from skullbase to vertex without
intravenous contrast.  Coronal and sagittal reformats were reviewed. 
Additional acquisitions were also performed due to significant motion on
initial acquisition.  Despite this there is some persistent motion at the
skullbase.

COMPARISON:  ___.

FINDINGS:

There is no definite acute intra-axial or extra-axial hemorrhage, mass,
midline shift, or territorial infarct.  There is prominence of the ventricles
and sulci compatible with global volume loss similar to previous exam.  There
is also suggestion of encephalomalacia within the cerebellum suggesting prior
infarct.  The gray-white matter differentiation is preserved.  Mastoids and
paranasal sinuses are grossly clear.  Skull extracranial soft tissues are
unremarkable.

IMPRESSION:

No acute intracranial process given limitation of motion degraded scan despite
multiple attempts.

CHEST RADIOGRAPH PERFORMED ON ___ 

___.

CLINICAL HISTORY:  Hypotension, assess pneumonia.

FINDINGS:  AP upright and lateral views of the chest were provided.  A
vascular stent is again noted in the region of the SVC, left brachiocephalic
vein.  There is blunting of the right CP angle which could indicate a small
effusion.  No overt signs of edema or pneumonia.  The cardiomediastinal
silhouette is stable.  Bony structures are intact.  Degenerative changes again
noted at the left glenohumeral joint.

IMPRESSION:  Small right pleural effusion.  Otherwise unremarkable.

HISTORY:  ___ year-old man with end-stage renal disease and complicated
hemodialysis access. His left upper extremity arteriovenous graft is
thrombosed. Graft angiography and thrombectomy is requested.  

COMPARISON:  Multiple reports and imaging studies dating back to ___ were
reviewed, which revealed difficulty with central line placement in the
internal jugular veins.  Recently, successful access was achieved from a
femoral approach.

OPERATORS:  Dr. ___ (attending), Dr. ___ fellow).

TASKS:
1.  Left AV graft access under ultrasound guidance, fistulagram with central
venogram.
2. Thrombolysis with Angiojet.
3. Thrombectomy with Trerotola device and ___ balloon catheter.
4.  Angioplasty with 6 and 7 mm balloon catheters.
5.  Placement of a right great saphenous to common femoral dialysis catheter.

MEDICATIONS: The patient received 100 mcg of fentanyl and 2 mg of Versed in
divided doses over a 5 hr period.  During the procedure the patient
experienced intense itching, and was given 50 mg of Benadryl in two doses. 
The patient was also administered 6,000 units of heparin in two doses over the
5 hour procedure time.  1% lidocaine was administered in the skin for local
anesthesia.  A total of 115 mL of contrast was given IV.  Hemodynamic
parameters were monitored throughout the procedure.

TOTAL FLUOROSCOPY TIME: 32 minutes (131 mGy).

PROCEDURE IN DETAIL:  

After explaining the risks, benefits, and alternatives, informed written
consent was obtained.  The patient was transferred to the fluoroscopy table in
the supine position, and the left arm was prepped and draped in the usual
sterile fashion.  Access to the left arteriovenous graft was obtained under
ultrasound guidance using standard micropuncture technique in antegrade and
retrograde directions.  Pre- and post- access images were obtained. 
Ultrasound revealed an occluded left upper extremity brachiobasilic graft.

An angled Glidewire was passed centrally, through the thrombosed graft and
into the right atrium.  Some difficulty was encountered when attempting to
navigate through the central venous brachiocephalic/SVC stent.  Next,
venography was performed peripherally and centrally to evaluate the entire
outflow tract.  A stenosis was noted both centrally around the region of the
anterior first rib and clavicle, and filling defects were noted in the left
upper extremity along the outflow tract from the graft to the left axillary
vein.  The decision was made to instill t-PA into the clot using the Angiojet
thrombectomy set.  8 mg of tPA was administered along the thrombosed portion
of the graft. After waiting several minutes, some clot was removed via
syringe, following which there was a mild pulse within the graft.  The 6
___ sheath were exchanged for a 7 ___ sheaths, and a Teratola device was
used to carry out thrombectomy from the left axillary vein down to the most
peripheral access site.  Following this, additional clot was removed through
the sheath and pulsatility within the graft improved, however flow was still
sluggish.  A ___ embolectomy catheter was used to remove additional clot
within the graft by advancing across the arterial anastomosis and pulling into
the graft inflate.

A repeat venogram of the left upper extremity revealed persistent stenosis in
the outflow tract in the upper arm.  Angioplasty of the outflow tract was
carried out with a 6 mm x 4 cm Durado balloon.  Repeat venography was sluggish
and demonstrated a small segment of stenosis near the retrograde access site
of the outflow tract.  Repeat angioplasty was performed with a 7 mm x 4 cm
balloon, following which graft re-occlusion occurred.  At this point, it was
about 4 hours into the procedure, and the decision was made to stop
thrombectomy and place a tunneled central venous catheter for dialysis.  The
sheaths were removed, and ___ nylon pursestring sutures were placed at both
access sites.  

Due to a combination of prior difficulty and central stenosis, IJ access was
not attempted.  A tunneled catheter was inserted into the IVC via the right
great saphenous vein.  The right great saphenous vein was accessed using
standard micropuncture technique under ultrasound guidance, following local
anesthesia with 1% lidocaine.  A guidewire was placed, and used to measure the
distance to the IVC/RA junction.  After selecting the tunneling site, the
catheter was selected such that the tip was two vertebral bodies below the
IVC/right atrial junction (15 ___, 48 cm hemodialysis catheter, 43 cm tip
to cuff).  The catheter was then tunneled to the venotomy site, inserted
through a peel-away sheath, and positioned was confirmed with a fluoroscopic
spot image.  The catheter was flushed and aspirated without difficulty.  A
sterile dressing was applied.

FINDINGS:

1.  Left brachiocephalic/SVC stent. 
2.  Moderate focal stenosis of the left subclavian vein at the thoracic
outlet. 
3.  Thrombosis from the graft to the leftaxillary vein, temporarily cleared
during the procedure, which then reoccluded toward the end of the procedure. 
4.  Small/stenotic left common femoral vein.

IMPRESSION:

1.  Fistulagram/central venogram revealed a focal moderate stenosis of the
left subclavian vein at the thoracic outlet and complete thrombosis of the
left brachiobasilic arterivenous graft.
2.  Unsuccessful thrombectomy using Angiojet, Treratola, ___ embolectomy
catheter and angioplasty.
3.  Placement of a tunneled dialysis catheter via the right great saphenous
vein.  IJ placement was not attempted due to past history of difficult access
and the presence of a left brachiocephalic/SVC stent.
